howToUse: 1. Attach or paste your slides, textbook chapter, or subject modules alongside this JSON template.
2. Instruct the AI: 'Follow _aiPrompt strictly to generate a randomized Question Pool bank covering every topic proportionally.'
3. Upload the returned JSON in Quiz Manager -> Import JSON. Each student attempt will receive a fresh non-repeating batch of questionsPerAttempt items.
_aiPrompt.prompt:
You are an expert item-bank psychometrician and strict JSON generator for Quiz Platform. Using ONLY the attached slides, textbook chapter, or topic, create a large, balanced Question Pool in strict JSON format.

QUESTION POOL DESIGN GOALS:
- A Question Pool serves random non-repeating subsets ('questionsPerAttempt') to students on each attempt—so EVERY question MUST be completely self-contained! NEVER reference 'Question 3 above' or repeat near-identical rewordings of the same fact.
- Generate at least 15-25 diverse questions (2x to 3x 'questionsPerAttempt') evenly distributed across every slide/sub-topic.
- Mix cognitive levels and question types ('multiple-choice', 'code-output', 'text', 'ordering', 'matching') so every random draw feels fair, varied, and challenging.
- Balance option lengths across all 4 multiple-choice options; every distractor must stem from a plausible student error (off-by-one, swapped definition, wrong complexity class, wrong scope).
- Write crisp explanations (1-2 sentences) teaching the underlying principle and warning against the main misconception.

UI & TEXT RENDERING RULES (CRITICAL):
- Question text, options, orderingItems, matchingPairs, and explanation use KaTeX math ($...$ inline, $$...$$ block, double-escaped backslashes \\ in JSON) and plain text ONLY.
- NEVER include raw Markdown (**bold**, *italic*, ### headings, ```code fences```, or `inline backticks`) in any text/option/explanation field because the renderer shows literal symbols.
- Put code snippets exclusively in 'codeSnippet' with clean \n line breaks.
- Keep 'orderingItems' in exact correct order (concise items <= 65 chars). Keep 'matchingPairs' clean (<= 35 chars left, <= 65 chars right).

STRICT JSON OUTPUT:
- Return ONLY valid raw JSON matching { "quizzes": [ { ... } ] }. Set "quizType": "pool", "isQuestionPool": true, appropriate "questionsPerAttempt" (typically 5-10), and omit '_aiPrompt'.

QuestionPoolQuiz.title: string (required)
QuestionPoolQuiz.description: string (required; state pool size & sampled attempt size)

QuestionObject.part: string (topic/slide tag so admins can audit topic coverage)
QuestionObject.question: string (self-contained prompt; $KaTeX$ allowed, NO raw markdown)
QuestionObject.options: string[] (for multiple-choice [4] or optional code-output choices)

questions.question: Which linear data structure enforces First In, First Out (FIFO) ordering for insertions and removals?
questions.explanation: A Queue enqueues items at the rear and dequeues from the front in FIFO order, whereas a Stack follows Last In, First Out (LIFO).

questions.question: What is the guaranteed worst-case lookup time complexity in a height-balanced Binary Search Tree such as an AVL or Red-Black Tree with $N$ nodes?
questions.explanation: Rebalancing rotations bound tree height to $\Theta(\log N)$, preventing degenerate $O(N)$ chains.

questions.question: Which JavaScript keyword declares a block-scoped variable binding that cannot be reassigned after initialization?
questions.explanation: The const declaration creates a block-scoped read-only binding reference, unlike let (reassignable) or var (function-scoped).

questions.question: Order these sorting algorithms by their worst-case asymptotic time complexity, from fastest to slowest (or fewest guarantees):
orderingItems: Merge Sort - O(N log N) worst case
Heap Sort - O(N log N) with O(1) space
QuickSort - O(N log N) avg, O(N^2) worst
questions.explanation: Merge Sort and Heap Sort guarantee $O(N \log N)$ worst-case time; QuickSort is $O(N \log N)$ on average but degrades to $O(N^2)$ on bad pivots; Bubble Sort is quadratic in both average and worst cases.

questions.question: Match each relational database schema term with its exact architectural purpose:

matchingPairs.right: Links a row to a key in another table

questions.explanation: Keys enforce entity and referential integrity, indexes trade write overhead for fast reads, and normalization structures dependencies cleanly.

questions.question: In Brewer's CAP Theorem for distributed data stores, what property does the letter C stand for?
questions.explanation: CAP stands for Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance—a partitioned distributed store must choose between linearizable Consistency and Availability.

questions.question: What boolean value is printed to stdout by this Python snippet?
questions.explanation: Empty Python sequences and collections ([], {}, '', set()) evaluate to False in boolean context.

questions.question: Which connectionless transport protocol prioritizes low latency over delivery guarantees and packet ordering?
questions.explanation: UDP (User Datagram Protocol) skips handshakes and retransmission overhead, making it ideal for real-time audio, video, and multiplayer games.

questions.question: What is the auxiliary call-stack space complexity of recursive Depth-First Search (DFS) on a tree of maximum height $H$?
questions.explanation: DFS only keeps the current root-to-leaf path on the recursion stack, consuming $O(H)$ space.
